en: Aiṃ 5 Thrauṃ! To the goddess Dambhakī and the Kṣetrapāla Mahādhvāṅkṣa of Prastaradvīpa, [I offer] the sandals.
Aiṃ 5, the sandals for the corpse-impregnated seat.
Aiṃ 5 Yāṃ, [I offer] the sandal to the Yoginīs.

Aiṃ 5! To whichever Yoginīs there may be—those born of the *pīṭhas*, those born of the *kṣetras*, those who are innate (*sahajā*), those born of enjoyment (*jogajā*), those born of the womb (*garbhajā*), and those born of the *kula*;

to whichever Yoginīs there may be—the *khecarīs*, *bhūcarīs*, *gocarīs*, and those consisting of one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine syllables; to those who move upon the earth, and to all others as they have arisen, [I offer] this *bali*.
Take [it] twice! Svāhā!
Aiṃ 5, the sandals for the seat of the pretas.
Aiṃ 5 Hskhphreṃ, the sandals of Śrī Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī. The offering.
Aiṃ 5, the sandals for the one seated upon the crucible.
Aiṃ 5 Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ! To the venerable Lord of the Kula-gaṇas, the sandals! Wealth! Offering!
The rites beginning with the invocation (āvāhana).
[Perform] the *caṇḍatarjanī-yoni-bindu-gajamudrā* and recite: *śrīṃ hrīṃ svāhā* ten times; *thrauṃ svāhā* ten times.

In the center of the circle, Gaurī holds Kumāra, the son of her son, supported by the sky; and Gaṇeśa, who removes obstacles and dispels the fear of misfortune, who has assumed the fierce form of Caṇḍamuṇḍā and the Yoginīs,
his limbs adorned and worshipped with flowers, incense, lamps, meat, honey, and offerings.
Having worshipped the solitary ones, she bestows various enjoyments and liberation for the benefit of all.
May all that in the ritual procedure for the worship of the five garlands be completely fulfilled. Vindutraya (three dots). Invocation.
Within the maṇḍala of Śrī Saṃvarta, Kṛṣṇavīra [is present]. || 2 ||

I bow to that excellent Guru, the venerable Kujeśa Bhairava, by whom the fourfold system—consisting of the auspicious powers of Ānanda, Mā, Sṛṣṭi, and Nyāya; the fivefold group belonging to Akula and Kula; another sixfold group; another fourfold group of five; and yet again a fourfold group—has been emitted and perfectly integrated with the Maṇḍala. Aiṃ 5.
A sandal for the human-seat.

[The mantra] *vali*. Invocation, installation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, and flowers: *namaḥ*.
One should display the *tarjanī-daṇḍa-gaja-mudrā*. This is the *yoginī*.

Invocation, installation, sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers—obeisance! [Perform] the *yonimudrā*.
Invocation and so forth; the mudrā; the seat.

Homage to the one seated upon the pericarp (*karṇikā*). Homage to the one seated upon the lotus (*padmāsana*). Homage to the Dharma.
Homage to Knowledge. Homage to Dispassion. Homage to Sovereignty. Homage to Unrighteousness.

Salutation to Ignorance (Ajñāna). Salutation to Non-sovereignty (Avairājña). Salutation to Lack of Mastery (Anaiśvarya). Salutation to the Lion Throne (Siṃhāsana). Meditation (Dhyāna): "Oṃ Aiṃ 5. She who bears in her hands the seed-vessel of the apricot (*prajaṃbīja*), a skull, and a lotus, resembling gold in hue—she is proclaimed as Mahālakṣmī. Thus is the meditation. The triple *añjali* (joining of palms).

Aiṃ! O you who dwell in the northeastern direction, you whose terrifying form is that of Īśāna’s withdrawal, great being, together with your fire, along with your limbs, retinue, and attendants—accept this offering of flowers, incense, lamps, and worship as it has been presented by me; accept this oblation (*bali*) of honey, wine, and flesh! Bhuru 2, muru 2, la 2, kha 2, khāhi!
2 pacify, 2 hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Aiṃ 5! All the pīṭhas and upapīṭhas, as well as the gates and sub-gates, the fields and sub-fields, and the saṃdohas, are situated in every direction.
All the lords of yoginīs and yogavīras have assembled there.
This supreme great wheel is Śrīnātha, the bestower of boons upon me.
Those devotees who are dedicated to the teaching of the Goddess and intent upon worshipping the feet of the Guru.
O Goddess, the grace that bestows all accomplishments shall always abide within them.
O Menakā, O daughter of the Earth, when heroes and yoginīs gaze upon it, one should then offer the *bali* there according to the practice of the *samaya*.
May the hosts of Yoginīs, crowded with throngs of attendants, destroy the hearing, memory, mind, nourishment, flesh, fat, bones, and life-force of the wicked.
It is spoken of as being free from deceit and the like, as well as from bad dreams and other such ill-omened occurrences.
Among the syllables beginning with Oṃ, those three which are proclaimed as the essential cores are [as follows].
Indeed, the medicinal herbs are found in the cardinal and intermediate directions,
as well as in the earth, the netherworld, the cosmic egg, and in all other locations.
Practitioners whose selves are united with the yoga of the Yoginīs abide in truth.
The Siddhas, the Putrakas, the Ācāryas, and the Sādhakas sleep upon the ground;
the Goddess Vaṭajā assumes various forms and possesses diverse [powers].
May all of them, being well-pleased, always accept the offering.
Even though I have come to them for refuge, all of this shall yield fruit for them.
Whatever action has been performed by me, whether it be yet to come or already done.
My Caṇḍikā is satisfied by the offering of leaves and flowers.
May all actions be accomplished and all defects be pacified;
through the bestowal of auspicious power, I bow to the venerable syllable *Kū*.
Thus is the offering of the pledge (samayabali).
Aiṃ 5 Ajara, Apakumbha, and likewise Iḍācāra.
Indramūrti, Ulkāsya, Ūṣmāṇḍa, Ripusūdana, Muktataptakāya, Phalāpāda, Ekadaṣṭaka, Airāvata,
Caḍodyāmva, and the other, Oṣadhīśa.
Antaka, Arthavāhu, Kamala, Kharānana,
Gomukha, Ghaṇḍāloḍaṇa,
Caṇḍadhāraka, Cchaṭāṭopa, Jaṭālākhya, Ṛkāra, Bhaṭeśvara, and likewise Ṭaṅkapāṇi.
And another was Aṣṭānuvan, and Ḍāmara; Ṭarṭṭakarṇa at the end of the [section], and Taḍidbhāsthavira likewise; Dantu, Rodhana, and Nāgakarṇa who possesses fierce power.
Phetkāra, Vīrasiṃha, Bhṛkuṭīkṣoma, Meghabhāsura,
Yugānta, Raurava, Lamvoṣṭha, and likewise Vatsala.
Śukatuṇḍa, Ṣaḍālāsya, Sunāsa, Huḥuhu,
and likewise Kṣayāntaka— these are declared to be the fifty Kṣetrapālas.
The fifty *kṣetralakas* reside in the locations of the fifty syllables; however, the fourteen *kṣetrapālas* are devoid of the remaining syllables.
She dwells at Ekaliṅga uttering the sound "Huṃ," and in the terrifying cremation ground;
Mahālakṣmī resides in the dreadful forest, and Jvālāmukhī always dwells there.
Furthermore, she who has the face of a cat resides at the single banyan tree.
The sound of bells resounds in his cave-dwelling; he is clothed in the waters of lotus-beds;
at the confluence, he possesses a multitude of flowing streams; likewise, on the mountain, there are winds;
and in the mountain torrent, there is the treasure Maṇibhadra, with its water flowing down to the ears.
One should know that the jackal is like a master of wealth in the fields of flavor,
while the bee is remembered as one who dwells in gardens and sacrificial enclosures.
The sixty-four Mahāvīryas remain protecting the world;
there, one should always offer oblations (*bali*) and worship at that sacred field (*kṣetra*).
There, four—the king, the twice-born (*dvija*), and others—receive the oblation.

One who has eyes like those of a land-dwelling bird, is of poor conduct, and has wasted his sacrificial offerings; these four possess perpetual authority. Others are of barbarian appearance, with hair and limbs that are tawny and eyes that are reddish-brown.
Terrible and fierce, with fangs bared and blazing as they carry skull-bowls;
[they are worshipped] with saffron, camphor, sandalwood, musk, civet, fish, and *phalguṣa*; likewise with flowers, garments, umbrellas, lamps, and *guggulu* incense.
Bhāvitā, Mānasī, Ādyā, Kramapūjā, Parālāpā, Vanāṅgī, and Ḍalomikā;
Bhīṣaṇā, Mahānandā, and likewise Jvālāmukhī;
Piśācī, Hastinī, Yakṣanī, and Dhūrjaṭī.
Viṣabhakṣī, Sarvasiddhi, Tuṣṭi, and likewise Icchā;
Kuṃkārī, Bhāśvarī, Dīrghā, Dhūmrākṣī, Kalahapriyā, O Dear One; Mātaṅgī, Kākadṛṣṭi, and likewise Tripurāntakī.
The Rākṣasī of terrible roar, red-limbed and possessing universal forms,
fearsome, fierce, with emaciated limbs, devouring the forest;
Vīrabhadra, Mahākārī, Kālī, and Vikṛtānanā.
Brahmī, Vaiṣṇavī, Raudrī, Carcikā, and likewise Īśvarī.
Vārāhī, Nārasiṃhī, and Śivādūtī.
p. 21) With bells, musical instruments, songs, and so forth, [one should] always satisfy Kāma.
5 Oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ! Descend, descend, O [Name]! You who possess a mass of matted hair tawny like the field and time, the radiant three-eyed one, O Jvālāmukhī!
Accept, accept the fragrance, flowers, and the offering of oblations! In the form of Bhairava, bhuru bhuru, muru muru, kha kha, la la, hraṃ phraṃ!
Haḥ! To the Lord of the Great Ḍāmara, svāhā!
Aiṃ 5 Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantī,
Aparājitā, Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Bhīmā, Kalā, and Aṣṭakā.
Divya-yoginī, Mahāyoginī, Siddhiyoginī, Gaṇeśvarī, Śākinī,
Kālarātrī, Ūrdhvakeśī, Niśācarī, Gambhīrā, and Aghoṣaṇī— these are the sixty-four [Yoginīs].
p. 20b) O Goddess Mahāyoginī, may you always accept this offering!
Hrīṃ! O sixty-four Yoginīs, accept the offering! Accept! Grant total peace! Destroy all obstacles! Grant peace to all diseases! Hna Phaṭ Svāhā!

Aiṃ! O Brahmā, you who are the eternal ocean of the blood of the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa), ever-flowing, neither hot nor cold, black and red; you who cause the mountain of the flesh of bound souls to fall at the tip of the primordial age;
you who bring an end to sleep with the thunderbolt; you who are the destroyer of Kurukānaga; O Goddess Sambhō, arise in the dance of Tāṇḍava, desiring to strike the wheel!
And having herself bowed at his feet, she spoke again.
Whether above the cosmic egg, in the sky, on the surface of the earth, in the void, in the netherworld, in fire,

or wherever one may stand— be it in sacred fields, seats, or secondary seats— if one has offered flowers, incense, and other gifts while placing one's feet there, may the Goddesses, being ever pleased by that, grant us their favor.
May those worthy of worship by the lord of heroes protect [us] according to the rite of auspicious offerings.
For the sake of the accomplishment of all goals, O you who are smeared with wine and flesh, accept this offering of *bali* twice; fulfill my desire for peace, *hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*.
Aiṃ 5 Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ! Yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, vetālas, and kṣetrapālas;
likewise ḍākinīs, mālās, pūtanās, and kātapūtanās.
Those born of the sacred seats (pīṭha), those born of the fields (kṣetra), those born of the womb, and likewise those who are innate;
those born of yoga, those born of mantra, and especially those born of the kula;
others who assume various forms, and other yoginīs who are not [merely] voracious.

Those dwelling in various lands have gathered here in this circle; others who abide by the commitments (samaya) likewise desire the sacrificial offering (bali). They are satisfied by divine intoxicants, perfumes, flowers, and other such offerings.
Being satisfied, grant the fulfillment of the desired object to those who offer [oblations].
HNA 3 PHAṬ! GR̥HṆA 2 SVĀHĀ!
OṂ & HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ KHPHREṂ! And likewise, O Śivā Bhagavatī and Māyābhadrā.
Kiṅkiṇī, Vimalālī, Yamajihvā, Tvakṣakarṣiṇī,
Ghaṇṭhodarī, Coramātā, Kiṅkiṇī, and likewise Kākinī— may these,
along with Siddhilakṣmī, always accept the offering on the thirteenth day.
For the destruction of all obstacles and the warding off of all enemies, accept this offering for Śrī Siddhilakṣmī at the thirteenth confluence: *gṛhṇa 2 svāhā*. Aiṃ 5.
O you of one syllable, who take form at will, vast and expansive, in the seat of the net of the unborn, in the center of the hexagon within the seat called Jaya.

O Goddess of gods, I bow to you, who possess the movement of the triple path, whose form is like a *śṛgātaka* flower; to you, the Teacher, accompanied by the assembly of Siddhas, who in this Kali age are joined with the group of six, and who, together with the *ḍala-rakas*, are the innate (*sahaja*) nature of the fivefold [elements] and the rest.

Aiṃ 5! Whether in heaven, the intermediate space, or the ten directions of the world; at the base of the seven netherworlds; in a sacred field (*kṣetra*), a seat (*pīṭha*), a secondary seat (*upapīṭha*), or an uneven crossroads;
in a cremation ground (*śmaśāna*); for the sake of accomplishment (*siddhi*) at a tree, a mountain peak, a beautiful riverbank, a cave, a valley, a hollow, Pūrṇagiri, or likewise—

And in the excellent city of Oḍiyāna, in the preeminent Jālākhya-yoga, in the chief Kulapati-nagara, in Kāmarūpa, Surūpa, Ḍarjaṇyā, Maṭṭahāsa, Paṭpaṭaha, Ravīlāḍa-deśa, in the region of Pradeśa, at Śrīśaila, Pālijāta,
in the abode of Paśupati, at Hemavindhyāvala, in the illustrious Mokāvāḍa country, and on Marutpathagiri.
Of the ḍākinīs and śākinīs.

In Kashmir, in the land of Candra, in Draviḍa and Malaya, in Brahmavāha, Kuluta, Strīrāja, Iṣvakvaḍoka, Urasī, Virajaka, the noble Siddhikṣetra, in Erudya, in Pālijāta, on the peak of the Himagiri, in Eka, in Videśa, and in Priyāga.
Now, in this region of Saurāṣṭra, at Bhṛgukaccha, the city of Anahilapātaka, Kośala, and Ekāmraka...

In Karṇāṭaka, Aṅga, Vāmagadhapura, Varakarṇa, Kuvjaka, Kaliṅga, Vacchoma, Haṃsavāha, Himaraja, Patalepa, Pāṭala, the region known as Iḍogara, Agau, Hemātṛcakra, Ḍohara— the abode of the hosts of sages—
and Candradeśa; in Rāmaura, Puṣpanākhya, the mountain depths of Girigahira, Guhevākuha, and Siṃhanāda.

In the place called Vaṅga, at Bhomanāda; in Śivapura, at Nagalebhadramūla; in Jayākhya, at the foot of the Prabalagiri mountain under the single umbrella known as Śrīvidyā; and in Yakṣakumbha and Laṅkā.

In Vārāṇasī, on the vast path of the triple-streamed river, on the pure road, in that tranquil place, amidst garlands of peace, or in the city within the Brahma-region of the caves of Mount Malaya; ||| 10 ||

In the auspicious body, at the root-place, in the dissolution of the city of primordial nature, in Siṃhakarṇa, in the direction of Īśāna, in the three-eyed one, in the center of the void upon the couch of the best of gods,

in the place called Gahvara— there, O Yoginī, may those Mothers, born of the egg, praised by various wise ones, all of them satisfied and well-perfected, praised by various wise ones, grant divine perfection.

May they grant the sword, the accomplishment of mantra, the illustrious [attainment] of the foremost city, flight through the sky, or yellow pigment (rocanā); may they grant the pacification of afflictions, the paralysis of enemies, victory over surrounding hosts, the immobilization of all spells, longevity, poetic skill, the treasure, the elixir, the pill, the sandals, the accomplishment of desires, and total subjugation.
Delighting in the script of the letter A, they are drenched in the blood of Aruru.

May she who wears a garland of skulls, meditated upon as the fierce goddess, dispel all fear at the gateway of the city of Nepal—she who, with the sound of the syllable *Oṃ*, causes the flight of wicked thieves, enemies, Māris, and hosts of malevolent planets.
*vauṃ cchauṃ oṃkārayantī* (She who utters the sound of *Oṃ*: *vauṃ cchauṃ*)
Laughing with repeated "ha ha ha ha" laughter, mocking, drinking, and dancing, the Mother of Mantra utters the sound "kili-kili-kili" while speaking in the Kaula tongue;

she is the withered one, whose form is desire, who possesses the syllables *ra*, *la*, *va*, and *pa*, who utters the sounds "hā hā ha" and the resonance of "kuṃ," and who arises as the Blue-throated One.
The heart-lotus, pure and stainless, is praised as the ocean.

Phreṃ! Phreṃ! Uttering the sound *phet*, devouring blood and fat with "ru! ru!", she lolls her tongue at the tip of her mouth with fury; "la! la! la! la! la!"—the creeper who causes [all] to run away, drinking [it all].

Kṛṣṇā, the messenger of Kāma, praised for her stainless qualities, who abides within the bindu and the end of nāda— she alone is capable of leading one across the shoreless expanse to the supreme state that bestows all accomplishments.
Prāgarbhā, Lokapālā, Gasapamanayutā, Pathivenuyuktā, Ṣaṣṭhasthā, Vinduyuktā, Kulakamalaratā, Tāriṇī, and she known as Kuṇḍalā—
the renowned Rudra-śakti, Bhīṣaṇī, and Bhadrakālī— may they all grant auspiciousness.
Kāṃ Kīṃ Kūṃ—she whose form is desire, who has entered the lineage of Akula, devouring those who harbor hatred.
Some are called Śrīkubjikā; others are the supreme Vāmadivya and the unerring Cāmuṇḍā. On the path of Kaula, there is Kaulinī, who consists of the lotus of the Kula;
she is known as Koṅkaṇā, whose abode is manifest on the path of Vāma, and whose body is the *bindu*.
Oṃ! She who is established in the syllable Oṃ or in the maṇḍala as the essence of Akula within the fire-wheel (agnicakra),
seated upon the lap of Śrīnātha, praised by the assembly of the most excellent sages,
she is the Goddess of terrifying form, the Mother of the World.

May Śrīnātha, who protects the faces of all [the deities] beginning with Śiva, protect the wheel. And may she known as Nvikā, who is worshipped by Śrīkaṇṭha, accompanied by Turyagā, established in the central liṅga, filling the seat (pīṭha), her radiant energy flashing like a firebrand, arisen from the Kaula path— [may she protect it].

I bow with devotion to the Goddess known by the name Śrī Kuvjikā, who possesses the movement of the triple-path (tripathagati), who is present in the three eyes, who manifests her abode through the modes of night, and who is differentiated by the beginning and end of the fivefold [categories].
May that Śrī Kuvjikāmva— black-hued, possessing a black form, with a most resonant voice, terrifying, and devouring— reveal to me the unfailing, divine flood of great gnosis.
hrīṃ glūṃ hrīṃ slūṃ hrīṃ plūṃ hrīṃ mlūṃ hrīṃ nlūṃ hsauḥ hsphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ||
Bestow supernatural power; bestow accomplishment; bestow knowledge; bestow longevity; bestow wealth; bestow grain; bestow prosperity.
Accept this offering, accept it! O you whose food is nectar, svāhā!
In the entire seat of mantras, forgive me for what has been said and what has not been said; O Giver of Boons, svāhā!
The worshipper, with palms joined in reverence, [should perform] the root-mantra [recitation] three times. [Then follows] the six-limbed worship (ṣaḍaṅgapūjā).
[Perform] the invocation and so forth; one should display the cow-mudrā and the womb-mudrā.
